brief.situation: You lead incident response at Calder Credit Union, a fictional lender. At 14:00 the SIEM correlates a web server reading member records in bulk with an egress spike to an outside address. Run the incident through to recovery: contain it, keep the evidence, report it to the people who decide, remediate, restore the service and set up the lessons learned.
handover: You may isolate hosts, block traffic, order images and rebuilds, and convene the incident response team. The CIO decides on outages beyond the web tier; legal counsel decides on notifications.
Online banking runs on WEB02 and WEB03 behind a load balancer, with the member database on DB01.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you close the incident you notify, record it and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Ten minutes until the web shell is copied to WEB03 is the author's figure.
Twenty minutes until the second transfer is the author's figure.
Forty minutes until the whole table is out is the author's figure.
Ten minutes from restoring an unpatched server to its reinfection is the author's figure.
Briefing the team, the CIO and counsel within the first hour is the author's teaching figure, not a legal deadline.

triageSiem.label: Review the SIEM correlation and WEB02's web logs

effects.log: You pull the correlated events and WEB02's web log.

effects.finding: A .php file uploaded through the avatar feature at 13:31 is a web shell; the app account behind it is paging through the member table and sending it to 203.0.113.88.

scope.label: Scope: search every web server for the same file and requests

effects.log: You search the web tier for u_7.php and the attacker's requests.

effects.finding: {isNull(web3At) ? "Only WEB02 has the file." : "WEB03 has it too, copied from WEB02."}

activate.label: Activate the incident response team and brief the CIO

effects.log: The team is convened and the CIO is briefed: what is happening, what you are doing, what decisions may need the CIO.

isolateWeb2.label: Isolate WEB02 from the network (EDR containment, kept powered on)

effects.log: WEB02 is cut off but running, so its memory is intact. Online banking runs on WEB03 alone.

isolateWeb3.label: Isolate WEB03 (online banking goes down)
isolateWeb3.available: not busy and isNull(web3IsoAt) and (not isNull(web3At))

effects.log: WEB03 is cut off. Online banking is down until a clean server is back.

blockEgress.label: Block 203.0.113.88 and all web-tier outbound except the payment gateway

effects.log: Outbound from the web tier is limited to the payment gateway; 203.0.113.88 is blocked.
DB01 goes down: the transfer stops, and so do branches, ATMs and card authorizations. Its memory is gone.

image.label: Capture WEB02's memory and a disk image, hash them, start chain of custody

effects.log: Memory and disk are captured and hashed; the chain-of-custody form names who holds them.

rebuild.label: Rebuild WEB02 from the gold image

effects.log: WEB02 is rebuilt from the gold image. {isNull(imagedAt) ? "Nothing was captured first: the attacker's tools and the server's memory are gone." : "The images are already in the case."}

patch.label: Deploy the vendor fix for the upload flaw to every web server image

effects.log: The fix is in the gold image and on every web server; uploads now accept images only.

restore.label: Bring online banking back on the rebuilt WEB02
restore.available: not busy and isNull(restoredAt) and (not isNull(rebuiltAt))

effects.log: Online banking is back. {isNull(patchAt) ? "The upload flaw is still there." : "The flaw that let them in is fixed."}

effects.log: Counsel has the facts so far and will decide on notifications and regulators.

effects.log: A notice goes up before the scope is known or counsel has decided; it will need correcting.

writeup.question: For the incident report: how you contained it, what you kept and reported, and how you recovered without letting it back in.

parts.label: Response and mitigation
parts.criteria: Isolates WEB02 (kept running) and cuts the egress path quickly, scopes the web tier and isolates WEB03 if found; does not power off the database, which stops every channel and loses memory.
parts.modelAnswer: Isolated WEB02 without powering it off and blocked outbound to all but the payment gateway within minutes, then scoped the tier for the same file.

parts.label: Evidence and reporting
parts.criteria: Captures memory and disk with hashes and chain of custody before the rebuild; activates the team, briefs the CIO and gives counsel facts early, leaving notification decisions to counsel.
parts.modelAnswer: Imaged WEB02's memory and disk with hashes and custody before rebuilding; convened the team, briefed the CIO and gave counsel the data types, count and times within the hour.

parts.label: Recovery and lessons
parts.criteria: Remediates the root cause (the upload flaw) before returning service; plans a blameless lessons-learned review with owners and dates.
parts.modelAnswer: Patched the upload flaw in the image and on every server before bringing banking back, and scheduled a blameless review with owners and dated actions.

expertPath.text: Read the correlation: a web shell exporting the member table. Convene the team and brief the CIO. Isolate WEB02, keep it powered on.
Block the egress; image WEB02's memory and disk with hashes and custody; brief counsel; scope the web tier.
Patch the upload flaw in the image and every server, rebuild WEB02, then restore banking.
Notify the CIO, counsel and the risk chair; record the root cause; schedule a blameless review with owners and dates.

handled.headline: Good: the whole life cycle, in order
handled.body: Detection, response, mitigation, reporting, recovery, remediation and lessons learned, each in its place: contain first, preserve before you rebuild, fix before you restore.

handledLate.headline: Recovered, with gaps
handledLate.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what cost you: slow containment, a second host or transfer, late reporting, or service not restored.

exfiltrated.headline: The data left first
exfiltrated.body: Investigating before isolating gave the transfer time to finish. Isolate and cut egress first; investigate on the images.

reinfected.headline: Back in through the same door
reinfected.body: A rebuild removes the attacker's files, not the flaw they used. Remediate the root cause before restoring service.

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence rebuilt away
evidenceLost.body: Capture memory and disk, hash them and start custody before anything is rebuilt or wiped.

leftOpen.headline: A server was left holding the shell
leftOpen.body: Scope the whole tier; a copy on a second server keeps the attacker in after you close.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No incident report was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Contain first: isolate WEB02 without powering it off and cut web-tier egress to the payment gateway only, then scope the tier and isolate any other copy. Capture memory and disk with hashes and chain of custody before any rebuild. Activate the team, brief the CIO, and give counsel facts early; notification decisions are counsel's. Remediate the root cause (the upload flaw) in the image and on every server before restoring service, then hold a blameless lessons-learned review with owners and dates. Powering off the database is disproportionate: it stops every channel and loses volatile evidence.
